speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the number of passengers arriving at Changi Airport in 2024; (b) what are the maximum capacity utilisation rates of Changi Airport Terminals 1 to 4 respectively in 2024; and (c) whether an update can be provided on the construction of Terminal 5 in view of the capacity utilisation rates of the other terminals.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Terminal 5 will enhance our passenger handling capacity and strengthen Singapore’s status as a leading air hub.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Can I ask the Minister, currently, based on the projection for the whole of 2024, will the passenger volume exceed pre-pandemic period?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Lastly, I would like to ask the Minister, we know the Jeju Air incident is a very sad incident.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Ang is right that we do need to prepare for this increase in passenger volumes.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If Changi does well, these passenger volumes will continue to grow.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Before Terminal 5 is ready, it will have to rely on the existing handling capacity of Terminals 1 to 4.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We look at aviation as a growth sector, which can provide many good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) is also undertaking a sectorial manpower study together with our tripartite partners to see how we can attract, retain and prepare our workers to be ready for this future growth.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are very sad to learn about this incident.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We convey our deepest condolences to the victims and their families.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The South Korean authorities are currently doing their investigations.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will review and take the necessary preventive actions as more information about the incident becomes available.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Based on the information that is currently available, the severity of the outcome was worsened because of the presence of a concrete structure at the end of the runway.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think there are some videos on social media showing the crash and how the plane ran into this concrete wall.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: All equipment that are required for air navigation purposes that are located near our runways are designed to break off in the event of a collision.
